title: GelCam: A Gel-Based Imaging Sediment Trap
summary: GelCam combines a gel-based sediment trap with time-lapse imaging to observe sinking particles and estimate their carbon flux.
coverAlt: GelCam schematic showing the sediment trap tube, gel layer, LED ring, and upward-facing camera

items.label: Capture particles.
items.text: Sinking particles enter the sediment trap tube and settle into a clear gel layer at the bottom.

items.label: Preserve particle shape.
items.text: The gel holds particles in place and helps preserve their shape for imaging and later sample analysis.

items.label: Record time-lapse images.
items.text: An upward-facing camera beneath the gel and an LED ring record newly arrived particles at regular intervals.

items.label: Quantify what arrives.
items.text: Image analysis identifies, tracks, and classifies particles to estimate arrival rates, particle-size distributions, and carbon flux.

body.alt: GelCam cutaway showing the trap tube, clear gel layer, LED ring, and upward-facing camera
body.caption: GelCam’s sediment trap and imaging components.

items.label: When:
items.text: When particles arrive and whether flux varies between day and night or during short-lived events.

items.label: What:
items.text: The size, shape, and type of arriving particles, including marine aggregates and fecal pellets.

items.label: How much:
items.text: Particulate organic carbon (POC) flux estimated from particle images and empirical carbon-content relationships. Conventional sediment trap measurements provide a check on these estimates.
